_note: Draft English of Saadia's JA Tafsir on Bereshit 39 (Joseph in Potiphar's house). Saadia-specific: v.1 'אלאעראב' = 'the Bedouins' (Saadia identifies the Ishmaelites with Arab Bedouins); v.9 'אלסייה אלעצ'ימה' = 'the great evil'; v.14 'ליתלעב בנא' = 'to make sport of us' (Saadia's gloss for לצחק בנו).

translations.1: And Joseph was brought down to Egypt; and Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh, the chief of the executioners, an Egyptian, bought him from the hand of the Bedouins who had brought him down there.
translations.2: And God was with him; and he was a successful man; and he settled in the house of his Egyptian master.
translations.3: And when his master saw that God was with him, and that everything he did, God made succeed in his hand,
translations.4: he found favor with him, and served him; and he appointed him over his household, and all that he had he placed in his hand.
translations.5: And from the time he appointed him over his household and all that he had — God blessed the Egyptian's house on account of Joseph; and the blessing of God was upon all that he had, in the houses and in the fields.
translations.6: And he left all that he had in his hand; and he did not concern himself with anything that was with him, except the food which he ate. And Joseph was beautiful both of form and of appearance.
translations.7: And after these things, the eyes of his master's wife were upon Joseph; and she said: 'Lie with me.'
translations.8: But he refused, and said to her: 'Behold, my master does not concern himself with me as to what is in the house; and all that he has, he has placed in my hand.
translations.9: And he is no greater in this house than I; and he has not withheld anything from me, except you — for you are his wife. How then can I do this great wickedness, and sin against God?'
translations.10: And as she spoke to him day by day, and he did not accept from her — to sleep beside her, to be with her —
translations.11: it was on a certain day, that he came into the house to do some work that was his; and no man of the household was there.
translations.12: And she caught hold of his shirt, saying: 'Lie with me.' And he left his shirt in her hand; and he fled, and went out into the street.
translations.13: And when she saw that he had left his shirt in her hand and fled into the street,
translations.14: she called to the people of her household, and said to them: 'Look — how he has brought us a Hebrew man to make sport of us! He came to me, to lie with me; and I called out with a loud voice.
translations.15: And when he heard me lifting my voice and calling, he left his shirt in my hand and fled, and went out into the street.'
translations.16: And she set his shirt by her, until his master came home.
translations.17: And she said to him: 'In just this manner came to me the Hebrew slave whom you brought us, to make sport of me.
translations.18: And when I lifted up my voice and called, he left his shirt in my hand, and fled into the street.'
translations.19: And when he heard her words which she said to him: 'Thus did your slave do to me' — his anger flared.
translations.20: And he took him, and placed him in the prison — the place where the king's captives were held; and he stayed there in the prison.
translations.21: But God was with him; and He inclined kindness toward him, and granted him favor in the eyes of the chief of the prison.
translations.22: Until the chief of the prison set under his hand all the prisoners who were in the prison; and all that they did there, he was the one to manage it.
translations.23: And the chief of the prison would see nothing wrong with him in anything; for God was with him; and whatever he did, God made succeed.
